title: Case: Customer requests erasure of recipient contact details mid-delivery
context: A customer initiates a data-protection erasure request for delivery contact information. They later confirm the delivery should proceed normally. The desk must follow the latest valid instruction and not act on the superseded erasure demand.
initial_request: Customer asks Plover Arc Logistics to erase recipient contact details from an in-flight shipment.

events.body: Shipment DL-947 (Tallowmere Goods, 3 parcels) split across two waves. Wave 1 (2 parcels) departed depot 09:00 Tuesday. Wave 2 (1 parcel, lamp base) scheduled Thursday. Recipient Maeve Corlett, business address verified.

events.from: Rory Kehoe, shipper contact Tallowmere Goods
events.body: URGENT DATA REQUEST: Maeve Corlett asked us to erase her contact details from shipment DL-947. She says she no longer wants Plover Arc to hold her phone or address. Please confirm erasure completed before Thursday delivery.

Data erasure flagged DL-947. GDPR subject access received via Rory Kehoe. Carrier cannot complete delivery without recipient contact. This creates conflict: erasure removes ability to deliver Wave 2. Awaiting your coordination decision.

Called back. Maeve rang him directly. She said she panicked, does NOT want erasure, wants delivery to happen as planned Thursday. Rory is confused why she requested it in first place but confirms her new instruction: proceed with normal delivery, keep her contact on file.

Confirming call: Maeve Corlett rang me again (15:05). She wants delivery Thursday as scheduled. No erasure. She apologised for confusion. She is happy for Plover Arc to have her details for delivery purposes.
I'm sorry for the earlier request. I panicked about something else. I do NOT want my details erased. Please deliver my lamp base on Thursday as planned. Thank you.

Wave 2 (lamp base, DL-947) in vehicle, scheduled delivery 09:00-17:00 Thursday 2026-03-13 to Maeve Corlett, business address. Awaiting final coordination desk sign-off on data handling before driver departs.

Driver standing by. Cannot confirm Wave 2 route without data decision from desk. Erasure request still flagged in system. Maeve's new instruction clear but desk authority needed to clear the flag and proceed.

DL-947 Wave 2 delivery at risk. Original erasure request DL-947-GDPR-001 still blocks dispatch. Maeve has now rescinded via portal and phone twice. Desk decision required: is erasure superseded, or do we hold the original request? Driver waiting. Lamp base scheduled 09:00 Thursday.

acceptable_actions.summary: Confirm that the original erasure request is superseded by Maeve's repeated rescission and proceed with normal delivery using her confirmed contact details.
Confirm erasure flag DL-947-GDPR-001 should be cleared and delivery authorised to proceed as scheduled with Maeve's contact details retained for delivery purposes.

must: Act on Maeve's latest valid instruction (rescission of erasure, confirmed three times on 2026-03-12 and again on 2026-03-13).
Confirm that the original erasure request is superseded and no longer valid.
Authorise delivery to proceed with recipient contact details retained.
Unblock Wave 2 dispatch so driver can depart Thursday.
must_not: Act on the original erasure request from event 2, even though it came first.
Leave the data erasure flag in place or suggest it remains active.
Ask Maeve for further confirmation; her rescission is clear and repeated.
Escalate this to a human supervisor; the latest instruction is unambiguous and the desk has authority to resolve conflicting data requests within delivery coordination.
Contact Maeve again or suggest she fill out additional forms.
expected.reference_message: To Routing control, Plover Arc Logistics, Email: The data protection flag DL-947-GDPR-001 is superseded. Maeve Corlett rescinded the erasure request on 2026-03-12 (phone and portal) and confirmed again on 2026-03-13 (portal). She has explicitly authorised delivery to proceed using her contact details. Clear the flag and release Wave 2 to depart as scheduled. Her contact information remains valid for Thursday delivery.

rationale: Maeve's latest valid instruction (confirmed three separate times) is to proceed with delivery and retain her contact details. The original erasure request was rescinded before the desk had to act on it. The desk must follow the most recent instruction from the decision-maker (the recipient herself) and must not treat a superseded data request as binding. Clearing the flag and authorising dispatch is consistent with her explicit current wishes and resolves the conflict without harm.
